gap: No result ChatGPT got states what an hour of P1S backup costs per station: at the 100–130 W a 120 V P1S draws once warm (holmes4's measurement), the BLUETTI AC180 ($499, about 7.5 h) and Elite 200 V2 ($899, about 13.6 h) both cost about $66 per printing-hour, while the 288 Wh Elite 30 V2 ($289.99, about 1.9 h) costs about $154.
standout_why: I read the Bambu forum thread 'Which UPS for a P1S+AMS?' (cited in all three chats) and the 'P1S power Consumption' thread. The quick-start and tech-spec PDFs ChatGPT cited would not render as text. The forum threads give watt readings but no runtime or price for any power station; the only runtime is arekxyz's untested '30-45 min max' for an APC Smart-UPS 1500 VA at 230 V. ChatGPT's own answers and our current page work out hours at an assumed 150 W, not at the measured 120 V draw, and neither gives a price per hour of outage covered or says that the 1 kWh and 2 kWh classes cost the same per hour.
decides: This confirms a lithium station of 1 kWh or more as the outage pick and makes the choice between them a matter of runtime, not value. The AC180 and Elite 200 V2 both cost about $66 per printing-hour, so buy the Elite 200 V2 only if prints run longer than about 7.5 h, because it covers about 13.6 h, enough for an overnight print. A 288–300 Wh unit costs more than twice as much per hour and lasts under 2 h, so it suits flickers and short outages. Every 600 W station has about 1.7× headroom over the 120 V heat-up peak of about 350 W. The Tenergy T320 (200 W continuous) stays off the list.

findings.source_title: Power Interruption Alert! - Which UPS for a P1S+AMS? - Bambu Lab Community Forum
findings.note: From forum user holmes4 on 120 V: 'Once at temperature, the draw varies between 100 and 130W.' Steady-state printing given as about 120–130 W. I use 130 W as the duty point for every figure below.

findings.label: P1S heat-up peak at 120 V vs 240 V
findings.value: about 350 W at 120 V; over 1,000 W at 240 V
findings.source_title: Power Interruption Alert! - Which UPS for a P1S+AMS? - Bambu Lab Community Forum
findings.note: holmes4: the 120 V startup draw 'tops out at around 350' and the 240 V startup 'can exceed 1000W'. The bed runs on line voltage, which is why the peak is higher at 240 V. Also in this thread, breach10ck's 600 W APC at 220 V shut off on a 1,000 W bed spike. That failure applies to 220 V, not to US 120 V.

findings.label: Heat-up peak duration (owner log, 220 V)
findings.value: 850 W for the first 30–60 s, then 30–70 W (PLA)
findings.source_title: P1S power Consumption - Bambu Lab Community Forum
findings.note: comecome logged the draw every second in Home Assistant over a 2 h PLA print at 220 V. Other replies disputed the 850 W figure. It shows the peak lasts under a minute and adds almost nothing to the energy a print uses.
